record.original_question: Let k be a positive definite kernel on a compact domain X subset R^d, let H_k be the associated reproducing kernel Hilbert space, and suppose an unknown reward function f belongs to H_k with ||f||_{H_k} <= B. In the online setting, a learner sequentially chooses points x_1, x_2, ... in X, observes noisy rewards y_i = f(x_i) + epsilon_i with i.i.d. sub-Gaussian noise, and may choose each new point using all previous observations. If mu_n(x) and sigma_n(x) are the surrogate Gaussian-process posterior mean and standard deviation after n observations, what is the smallest possible growth rate in n of a confidence-width factor rho_n(delta) for which, with probability at least 1 - delta, the uniform bound |f(x) - mu_n(x)| <= rho_n(delta) sigma_n(x) holds for all x in X? In particular, can the existing online RKHS confidence interval be improved by an O~(sqrt(gamma_n)) factor, where gamma_n is the maximal information gain?

evidence.quote: In online learning problems, the observation points are collected sequentially. In particular, the observation point x_{i+1} is determined after all the values {(x_j , y_j )}^i_{j=1} are revealed.

Our open problem is concerned with improving this confidence interval. Open Problem. Under Assumption 1, in the online setting, consider the general problem of proving a confidence interval of the following form uniformly in x in X: |f(x) - mu_n(x)| <= rho_n(delta) sigma_n(x), with probability at least 1 - delta. What is the lowest growth rate of rho_n(delta) with n? In particular, is it possible to reduce the confidence interval width in Theorem 2 by an O~(sqrt(gamma_n)) factor?

artifact.category_tag: Kernel bandits and RKHS confidence intervals
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{X}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a positive definite kernel on a compact domain $\mathcal{X}\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, and let $\mathcal{H}_k$ denote the associated reproducing kernel Hilbert space with norm $\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal{H}_k}$. Fix $B>0$ and assume the unknown target $f\in\mathcal{H}_k$ satisfies $\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_k}\le B$. 

Consider the online (sequential) sampling setting: a learner chooses points $x_1,x_2,\ldots\in\mathcal{X}$ adaptively, where each $x_{i+1}$ may depend on the previous observations $\{(x_j,y_j)\}_{j=1}^i$, and observes $y_i = f(x_i) + \varepsilon_i$ with $\{\varepsilon_i\}$ i.i.d. zero-mean $R$-sub-Gaussian noise independent across $i$. Given a prior variance $\lambda>0$, define the surrogate Gaussian-process posterior mean and standard deviation after $n$ observations by
$$\mu_n(x) = k_n(x)^\top (K_n + \lambda I)^{-1} Y_n,\qquad \sigma_n^2(x) = k(x,x) - k_n(x)^\top (K_n+\lambda I)^{-1}k_n(x),$$
where $K_n=[k(x_i,x_j)]_{i,j\le n}$, $k_n(x)=[k(x,x_i)]_{i\le n}$, and $Y_n=(y_1,\ldots,y_n)^\top$. Let the maximal information gain after $n$ rounds be
$$\gamma_n = \max_{x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\mathcal{X}} \tfrac{1}{2}\log\det\!\bigl(I + \lambda^{-1} K_n\bigr).$$

For $\delta\in(0,1)$, a (uniform) confidence width factor $\rho_n(\delta)$ is admissible if, with probability at least $1-\delta$,
$$|f(x)-\mu_n(x)|\le \rho_n(\delta)\,\sigma_n(x)\quad\text{for all }x\in\mathcal{X}.$$

Determine the smallest growth rate of an admissible $\rho_n(\delta)$ as $n\to\infty$. In particular, decide whether the best known admissible factor of order $\widetilde{O}\!\bigl(B+R\sqrt{\gamma_n\log(1/\delta)}\bigr)$ can be improved by a factor of $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{\gamma_n})$, i.e., whether an admissible $\rho_n(\delta)$ of order $\widetilde{O}\!\bigl(B+R\sqrt{\log(1/\delta)}\bigr)$ (or otherwise free of the $\sqrt{\gamma_n}$ factor) exists in the online setting.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was posed as an open problem at COLT 2021. Subsequent work has obtained tighter bounds in restricted offline/pure-exploration settings (e.g., $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{\gamma_N/N})$ simple regret), but no resolution of the general online uniform confidence-interval question has been verified in the search results, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Open Problem: Tight Online Confidence Intervals for RKHS Elements (COLT 2021)
status_evidence.snippet: Formal posing of the open problem on whether online RKHS confidence intervals can be tightened by an Õ(sqrt(gamma_n)) factor.
status_evidence.claim: The question is formally a posed open problem from 2021.

status_evidence.title: Optimal Order Simple Regret for Gaussian Process Bandits (NeurIPS 2021)
status_evidence.snippet: Provides sharper confidence intervals for GP models in pure-exploration settings, yielding Õ(sqrt(gamma_N/N)) simple regret bounds.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists in non-online or pure-exploration regimes, but does not resolve the general online uniform-confidence question.
